newsitem.title: EGYPT: ING Barings tips Egypt's CIB.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings tips Egypt's CIB.

text.p: International securities house ING Barings said on Tuesday it would recommend buying into Egypt's Commercial International Bank (CIB) in the light of year-end results released on Sunday.
The bank, Egypt's largest in the private sector, reported 1996 net profits of 241.3 million pounds ($71.1 million) almost 11 percent up on 217.7 million in 1995.
ING Barings said the bank's ROAE (return on average equity) in 1996 was impressive at 25.1 percent against 24.0 in 1995 and its ROAA (return on average assets) was 2.6 percent against 2.2.
"For the current year we anticipate a further strong rise in both the loan and deposit growth, helped by the rapid expansion of CIB's retail network," it said.
"Looking ahead, it is also clear that CIB is positioning itself to win market share from the large, and still highly inefficient, state banks.

"After rising and falling sharply, the local shares currently trade fairly in line with the market at 14.7 times 1997 earnings. The GDRs however continue to trade at a discount to the local at 13.6 times 1997 earnings.
"We reiterate our belief that CIB remains an excellent market proxy and should be a core holding in any Egyptian portfolios. Buy the GDRs," it added.
The local shares closed on the Egyptian stock exchange at 76.25 pounds ($22.46) on Tuesday. ING Barings quoted the GDRs at $20.70 bid and $21.00 ask.

In ratings for three Egyptian banks announced on Monday, Moody's gave CIB a C for bank financial strength and Ba3/Not Prime for deposits. The bank financial strength rating for CIB was higher than for the other two -- Egyptian American Bank and Misr International Bank/MIBank.
